{{Short description|Criterion for existence of polynomial roots}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Heegner's lemma''' is a lemma used by [[Kurt Heegner]] in his paper on the [[class number problem]]. His lemma states that if
 
:<math>y^2=a_4x^4+a_3x^3+a_2x^2+a_1x+a_0 </math>

is a curve over a field with ''a''<sub>4</sub> not a square, then it has a solution if it has a solution in an [[field extension|extension]] of odd degree.
